title: Cello arco
notes:
The same instrument family as `bass/upright-pizz` with the bow on the string instead of a finger under it, which turns out to be a bigger difference than the instrument change would have been. Everything acoustic on this shelf is *plucked* — upright, nylon, sitar, jawari — so the low end has never once been able to hold a note. A chamber cue, a funeral, anything that wants the bass line to *sing* rather than to walk, had nothing.

**A bow is a sustain mechanism, so the envelope inverts.** Attack 90 ms against the pizzicato's 12: the bow has to grab the string and set the Helmholtz corner running, and that takes a real fraction of a beat. Sustain 0.85, because energy keeps arriving for as long as the arm moves — the plucked voice sustains at 0.35 and is already dying. Release 0.5, which is *shorter* than upright-pizz's 1.3 even though the box is the same size: lifting a bow damps the string, where releasing a plucked string does nothing at all. That inversion — slow in, held, quick out — is the whole articulation, and it is why this is not the pizz with a longer attack.

**The filter opens instead of collapsing.** Base 180 Hz, 2.6 octaves, but sustaining at 0.7 with a 140 ms attack on the filter envelope, so the note gets *brighter* under the bow and stays there. A plucked string is brightest at the instant of the pluck and darkens monotonically; a bowed one is the opposite, and getting this backwards is the fastest way to make a bowed patch sound like a plucked one with the attack turned up. `fatsawtooth12` at the source rather than the pizz's `fatsawtooth6` — bowing is a sawtooth by physics (the string sticks and slips once per period), and the bow keeps feeding the upper partials that a plucked string loses immediately.

**Vibrato is now load-bearing rather than a synth-tell fix.** Rate 5.2, depth 0.05, drift 0.5 — a cellist's actual hand, four times the width of the pizzicato's token 0.012. A held bowed note with stationary pitch is not a cello at all; on a plucked note nobody would notice.

**Body is a cello, not a double bass.** 100 Hz is the air mode (the double bass's is 60 — the instrument is smaller), 190 Hz the top plate, −4 dB at 420 Hz is the hollow between the modes, and 1.6 kHz is the bridge hill, which the pizz voice does not have at all because a plucked note has nothing left up there to excite it.

**Breath is rosin, not thwack.** 3.8 kHz at level 0.08 with a 30 ms follower, against upright-pizz's 1.6 kHz at 5 ms. A fast follower is a transient — the string slapping the fingerboard; a slow one is a *continuous* scrape that lives under the whole note, which is what a bow does. Same block, opposite reading, and it is the second reason these two never converge on the way to the speaker.

No amp, for the reason `bass/jones-jazz` established and every acoustic voice here inherits: the power stage is a fixed 0.18 distortion, and a bowed instrument with grit on it is a synth.

Auditioned on the bass étude. It will smear on the fast passage — a 90 ms attack cannot articulate sixteenths, and that is true of the real instrument. Pick it for half notes.
summary: Bowed low strings, the one bass that sustains. Chamber and funeral lines that sing rather than walk; too slow to articulate sixteenths.
